text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A faction in opposition party FORD-Asili led by Martin Shikuku has sacked party chairman Kenneth Matiba for failing to attend a party National Executive Council meeting convened to discipline him.
- The government says it is ready to discuss issues openly and rectify its shortcomings but says it will not accept dictatorial recommendations.
- The Eldoret International Airport in the Rift Valley is yet to open for commercial use.
- The umbrella protestant National Christian Council of Kenya asks the government to heed demands for constitutional reforms before the parliamentary and presidential elections.
- Nearly three million people -- about 30 percent of eligible voters -- have registered for the general elections scheduled for later this year.
- Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi confirms June 19 as the date for his 1997/98 state budget presentation to parliament.
- Twelve people die in a road accident along the Nairobi-Mombasa highway.
- Hawkers from the coastal town of Mombasa demonstrate against a constitutional reform rally scheduled for June 21.

- The Peaceful Assemblies Bill proposed by President Daniel arap Moi is just a recycled version of the unpopular Public Order Act and is meant to hoodwink Kenyans with its cosmetic changes, according to political analysts.
